headline_marked: 19 million users' data [[leaked from Pathao]], hackers demand $400k
headline: 19 million users' data leaked from Pathao, hackers demand $400k
summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen 133GB of sensitive user information, including NIDs and addresses, demanding a ransom payment to prevent its release.
details: A hacker group claims to have accessed the data of approximately 19 million Pathao users. The stolen information allegedly includes phone numbers, email addresses, NIDs, driving licenses, home addresses, and Facebook profiles.
The attackers are demanding $400,000 from Pathao to prevent the public release of this data. They claim to possess 133GB of information, comprising 250 million records and 591 databases.

Pathao confirmed in a statement that some personal information, including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by attackers. They stated that the situation was brought under control immediately after detection.

The company noted that users may experience temporary technical issues as they work to stabilize the system. Pathao has engaged external cyber security experts to secure their systems and will update relevant authorities according to regulations.
The cyber security incident was first brought to light by the platform 'Daily Dark Web' on X (formerly Twitter) on Wednesday, though the claim's full extent has not been independently verified.

Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha suggests that Pathao should immediately conduct an independent digital forensic investigation and preserve all digital evidence, including servers and access logs, to protect citizens' data.
caption:

A hacker group claims to have accessed the data of approximately 19 million Pathao users. The stolen information allegedly includes phone numbers, email addresses, NIDs, driving licenses, home addresses, and Facebook profiles.

The attackers are demanding $400,000 from Pathao to prevent the public release of this data. They claim to possess 133GB of information, comprising 250 million records and 591 databases.

Pathao confirmed in a statement that some personal information, including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by attackers. They stated that the situation was brought under control immediately after detection.

The company noted that users may experience temporary technical issues as they work to stabilize the system. Pathao has engaged external cyber security experts to secure their systems and will update relevant authorities according to regulations.

The cyber security incident was first brought to light by the platform 'Daily Dark Web' on X (formerly Twitter) on Wednesday, though the claim's full extent has not been independently verified.

Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha suggests that Pathao should immediately conduct an independent digital forensic investigation and preserve all digital evidence, including servers and access logs, to protect citizens' data.

headline_marked: Bangladesh signs [[15-year deal with DP World]] to operate NCT
headline: Bangladesh signs 15-year deal with DP World to operate NCT
summary: The agreement covers the operation and maintenance of the New Container Terminal (NCT) and its overflow yard, amid protests from port labor organizations.
details: Bangladesh has signed a 15-year concession agreement with DP World to operate the New Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port. The deal allows the Dubai-based company to manage and maintain the terminal and its overflow container yard.
The partnership aims to increase operational efficiency, modernize the terminal, and enhance the overall capacity of the port and logistics infrastructure.
The agreement was discussed during a meeting between the Prime Minister and a delegation led by DP World's Board of Directors Chairman Esa Kazim.
The Prime Minister also sought further investment from DP World in free trade zones and inland container depots to further boost trade and investment between Bangladesh and the UAE.
However, the deal has sparked protests from leftist groups and port labor organizations. Protesters have called for a mass hunger strike starting Monday, October 12, to oppose the agreement.
Police have already intervened to disperse protesters who erupted over the deal, leading to tense situations at the port area.
caption:
A 15-year deal has been signed to hand over the operation of the New Container Terminal to DP World, but port workers are fighting back.

Bangladesh has signed a 15-year concession agreement with DP World to operate the New Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port. The deal allows the Dubai-based company to manage and maintain the terminal and its overflow container yard.

The partnership aims to increase operational efficiency, modernize the terminal, and enhance the overall capacity of the port and logistics infrastructure.

The agreement was discussed during a meeting between the Prime Minister and a delegation led by DP World's Board of Directors Chairman Esa Kazim.

The Prime Minister also sought further investment from DP World in free trade zones and inland container depots to further boost trade and investment between Bangladesh and the UAE.

However, the deal has sparked protests from leftist groups and port labor organizations. Protesters have called for a mass hunger strike starting Monday, October 12, to oppose the agreement.

Police have already intervened to disperse protesters who erupted over the deal, leading to tense situations at the port area.
